title: U.S. House · Arkansas's 2nd District
area: Central Arkansas, including Little Rock, North Little Rock, and Conway.

context.text: Incumbent French Hill defeated Chase McDowell in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary. Chris Jones defeated Zack Huffman in the Democratic primary. Jones previously ran for Arkansas Governor in 2022, losing to Sarah Huckabee Sanders.

summary.text: French Hill is the Republican nominee and incumbent U.S. Representative for Arkansas's 2nd District, seeking re-election.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Vanderbilt University in 1975.
Worked as Deputy Assistant Secretary of the U.S. Treasury (1989-1991) and as senior policy advisor to President George H.W. Bush (1991-1993).
Worked as a senior advisor to Arkansas Governor Mike Huckabee in 2008.
Founded and chaired Delta Trust & Bank.

priorities.text: It cuts red tape, increases housing supply, and makes homeownership more attainable for families across Arkansas and the nation... This legislation strengthens community banks, modernizes building codes, and cuts red tape. More houses will be built, more families will enter the market, and homes across the country will be more affordable.

As a former community banker in central Arkansas, I know how important our Main Street banks are to our local economy... It right-sizes regulations for our community banks, freeing them up to lend so entrepreneurs can invest, businesses can grow, and families can build wealth.

positions.summary: Sponsored the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, enacted in 2026, which he describes as reducing regulatory barriers to new home construction and modernizing local zoning rules to increase housing supply.
positions.quote: It cuts red tape, increases housing supply, and makes homeownership more attainable for families across Arkansas and the nation.

record.text: Currently serves on the House Committee on Financial Services and the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence.
Sponsored the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, a bipartisan housing bill that reduces regulatory barriers to home construction and modernizes HUD programs; signed into law in July 2026.
Sponsored the Main Street Capital Access Act (H.R. 6955), which right-sizes bank capital regulations for community banks; passed the House 270-155-1 in July 2026.

candidates.name: Chris Jones

summary.text: Chris Jones is the Democratic nominee for Arkansas's 2nd Congressional District. He is an executive director and former engineering professor who was the Democratic nominee for Arkansas Governor in 2022, losing to Sarah Huckabee Sanders.

background.text: Born in Pine Bluff, Arkansas, the son of two preachers.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Morehouse College (1999) and a graduate degree and Ph.D. from MIT (2003, 2016).
Works as an executive director; was the 2022 Democratic nominee for Arkansas Governor.

priorities.text: Campaign site lists three pillars: "Affordability For All," "Accountability For All," and "Opportunity For All."
Describes his campaign as focused on expanding opportunity and strengthening communities, citing prior work on schools, jobs, and healthcare access.
priorities.quote: I'm a bridge builder, a fighter for us, and a visionary for the future of Arkansas. Our campaign is about expanding opportunity, strengthening our communities, and proving that when Arkansans come together, we can fly.

candidates.researchNotes: Jones has not completed a 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey for this race; his Ballotpedia page's quoted policy platform dates to his 2022 gubernatorial campaign and was not used here as a current position. Specific 2026 issue positions were not found beyond his campaign site's three named priorities.
